expert_proposals.title: Raise default_statistics_target 100->300 for skewed GetUserTweets selectivity
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=100 leaves coarse MCV/histogram resolution for the heavily skewed user_id predicate driving GetUserTweets (88% of terminal capacity); planner estimates stay coarse and per-call page work is not minimized.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88) with p50 171us and p99 1092us. Its predicate on user_id is highly skewed; at statistics target 100 the MCV list and histogram under-resolve the hot user_id values, so the planner's row estimate for the dominant template is coarse and it may pick a plan that touches more heap pages per call than necessary. Raising default_statistics_target to 300 triples histogram/MCV resolution for skewed columns, sharpening selectivity estimates and letting the planner choose the tighter index path. This is a planner/statistics knob, orthogonal to the WAL and predicate-lock bundles already tested; it targets the dominant transaction's per-call page work rather than commit-path queueing.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Finer user_id selectivity estimates should let the planner pick a tighter index path for the dominant GetUserTweets template, reducing pages touched per call and lowering its p50/p95 latency.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful transaction TPS as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy falls; effect bounded because the dominant cost is per-call index work, not commit path.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease; other transaction classes roughly unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Triple from 100 to 300 within safe [50,500]; 3x histogram/MCV resolution for skewed user_id while keeping ANALYZE cost bounded.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: column statistics resolution for skewed predicate selectivity

predictions.rationale: Finer MCV/histogram resolution for skewed user_id yields tighter index path and fewer pages per call.
Sharper selectivity estimates reduce worst-case page work for the dominant template.
Lower GetUserTweets terminal occupancy frees finite client terminal capacity for more completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If the dominant GetUserTweets plan is already index-only and insensitive to selectivity resolution, statistics target has no measurable effect and p50 stays flat.
If commit-path WAL sync (sync_average_ms ~0.13ms, wal_waiting_backends max 1) is the true limiter, GetUserTweets latency is unchanged and only WAL bundle knobs move TPS.

cross_domain_requirements: ANALYZE must run after the change so new statistics are visible to the planner before measurement.

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path: widen group-commit window and batch writer flushes
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a fixed per-commit stall that rarely collects siblings at 5 terminals, while wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces per-write flushing; WAL sync latency (0.13ms) and wal_wait persist.
expert_proposals.mechanism: The WAL commit path is the only storage-side anomaly: wal_waiting_backends max=1 with sync_average_ms=0.13 and write_average_ms=0.022, host_io stalls zero, so the cost is sync frequency/queueing, not disk saturation. commit_delay=100us is too short to collect the 5 terminals' commits yet still adds a fixed stall to every commit; commit_siblings=2 gates group commit too eagerly. Widening the collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets concurrent commits coalesce into one fsync, while wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) batches background writer flushes instead of flushing per write. Together these reduce syncs per transaction and drain the WAL wait queue, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88); reducing commit-path queueing shortens InsertTweet and mixed-transaction stalls, freeing terminal slots for the dominant read path.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps as WAL wait queue drains; bounded by client terminal saturation.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 and GetUserTweets p99 decrease slightly; overall p95 roughly unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window coalesces concurrent commits into fewer fsyncs, lowering average sync latency.
Batched writer flushes plus group commit drain the WAL wait queue.
Fewer commit-path stalls free terminal capacity for the dominant GetUserTweets path.

alternatives.statement: If the 500us window adds more stall than it saves, sync latency and TPS will not improve; a shorter window (200us) would then be preferred.
If WAL wait is incidental and terminal saturation is purely read-side, TPS stays flat despite lower sync latency.

cross_domain_requirements: wal_compression already on; no further WAL volume reduction available

expert_proposals.title: Coarsen predicate-lock promotion further: page 8->32, relation 4->16
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2 (default) force early SIRead promotion to coarser granularity; the r005 test raised them to 8/4 and cut locks_total.p95 by ~80% and GetUserTweets.p99 by ~47-72%, but the TPS prediction was refuted because the amplitude was too small to move the terminal-bound GetUserTweets path.
expert_proposals.mechanism: SERIALIZABLE SIRead locks are promoted to coarser granularity when per-page/per-relation caps are exceeded. r005 showed the promotion path is real: locks_total.p95 fell ~80% and GetUserTweets.p99 fell 47-72% with page=8/relation=4, yet TPS was inconclusive because the effect was within run-to-run noise. Raising the caps further (page 32, relation 16) keeps the same mechanism but with a larger amplitude, so the lock-bookkeeping reduction should be measurable in locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets.p99 while lock_waiting_backends stays at 0 (no true lock contention, only bookkeeping).
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets is the terminal-dominant transaction (terminal_capacity_fraction 0.88). Coarser SIRead locking reduces per-call lock bookkeeping on its read path, lowering its p99 and freeing terminal capacity.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small positive: successful_transaction_tps should rise modestly as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy drops; magnitude bounded by the 0.88 terminal fraction and the fact that lock bookkeeping is a secondary cost.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 should decrease; p50 roughly unchanged since promotion affects tail bookkeeping more than the median path.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x the r005 tested value of 8, within safe [0,256]; r005 showed -80% locks_total.p95 at 8, so 32 tests a larger amplitude of the same supported mechanism.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; higher value delays promotion to coarser granularity

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x the r005 tested value of 4, within safe [-2,4096]; positive cap of 16 relation-level locks coarsens promotion further than r005's 4.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; higher positive value delays relation-level promotion

predictions.rationale: Larger caps delay promotion, further reducing total SIRead lock count versus the r005 8/4 setting.
r005 already showed 47-72% p99 reduction at 8/4; larger amplitude should preserve or extend that direction.
Freed terminal capacity from lower GetUserTweets tail should translate to a small TPS gain; r005 was inconclusive at 8/4, so larger amplitude is the test.

alternatives.statement: If locks_total.p95 falls but GetUserTweets.p99 and TPS are unchanged, SIRead bookkeeping is not on the critical path and the terminal bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g. index scan cost).
If lock_waiting_backends.max rises above 0, coarser promotion is creating real serialization conflicts rather than reducing bookkeeping.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent sits at page=2/relation=-2 (defaults). r005 proved the promotion mechanism is real (locks_total.p95 -80%, GetUserTweets.p99 -47-72%) but was inconclusive on TPS due to small amplitude. This proposal keeps the same mechanism with a larger safe amplitude (page 32, relation 16) to make the TPS effect measurable.

nodes.label: Delayed SIRead promotion reduces per-txn predicate-lock bookkeeping
